guitar.modelsText: Messenger / Gibson Flying V (Grand Funk Railroad)
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: Mark Farner of Grand Funk Railroad is known to have used a Messenger guitar (aluminum-neck) and Gibson Flying V live.
guitar.notes: Reasonably documented for classic rock gear enthusiasts.

tone.target: bright AM-radio crunch with slight drive and tight attack
tone.profile: bright AM-radio crunch with slight drive and tight attack
tone.summary: A tight signal chain using a mild OD boost into a British combo amp model (UK 45 or UK 50) paired with a smaller cabinet to achieve the desired bright, punchy, and dry 60s radio crunch.

rig.name: Mark Farner - Some Kind Of Wonderful - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up background noise and maintain tight rhythm definition.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for clean/crunch tones.

blocks.purpose: Provide light breakup and the necessary 'crunch' without heavy distortion.

blocks.purpose: No dedicated distortion needed; the Green OD provides sufficient light breakup.
blocks.gap: The signal chain is kept simple as requested. No DST module is required.

improvements.summary: Replace the current 4x12 cabinet with a smaller, more vintage-appropriate speaker to enhance the dry, punchy 60s radio crunch.

proposals.reason: A smaller cabinet better matches the 'small combo' and dry, punchy 60s radio sound.
